## Design roles

Each part does a job for the person. These are the jobs, as questions the part answers.

<div class="odv-am-rolelist"><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Containment</b> What holds this?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Layering</b> What sits on top?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Hierarchy</b> What do you read first?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Readability</b> Can you read it?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Emphasis</b> Where does the eye go?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Meaning</b> What state is it in?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Affordance</b> Can you act on it?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Feedback</b> Did it respond?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Focus</b> Where is the keyboard?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Grouping</b> What belongs together?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Reach</b> Can you hit it?</span></div>

## How the decisions reach each part

Each part follows a chain: an answer about the product, the rule it set, the token that carries it, and the value you see. The numbers match the drawing.

<section class="odv-am-card" id="part-1"><div class="odv-am-img wide"><span class="odv-am-assetbox"><img class="odv-am-asset" src="/anatomy/brand-expressive/button/card-1.png" alt="Container: 1" loading="lazy"/></span></div><div class="odv-am-body"><header><i class="odv-am-n">1</i><b>Container</b><span class="odv-am-role" title="Can you act on it?">Affordance</span><span class="odv-am-role" title="Can you hit it?">Reach</span></header><ul class="odv-am-tree"><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Answer</b><div class="odv-am-main">Shape · What should control corners say? → Pill</div><div class="odv-am-why">Pill controls feel playful.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Answer</b><div class="odv-am-main">Accessibility · What is the smallest target? → Touch size</div><div class="odv-am-why">Visitors come from social posts on phones.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Answer</b><div class="odv-am-main">Spacing · How dense is the layout? → Spacious</div><div class="odv-am-why">Big space makes big moments.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Rule</b><div class="odv-am-main">For corners of buttons and inputs, use radius.control (pill). Don't use sharp corners.</div><div class="odv-am-why">Pills match the brand's round, playful shapes. Sharp corners would feel corporate.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Rule</b><div class="odv-am-main">For the smallest clickable thing, use size.control.default (touch). Don't use a compact control.</div><div class="odv-am-why">Most visitors arrive on phones, and a compact control is too small for a thumb.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Token</b><div class="odv-am-chain"><code>size.control.default</code><span>→</span><code>height</code><span class="odv-am-val">3.25rem</span><span class="odv-byscheme" title="Its value changes by scheme. The part is the same in every scheme."><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="11" height="11" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m11 10 3 3"/><path d="M6.5 21A3.5 3.5 0 1 0 3 17.5a2.62 2.62 0 0 1-.708 1.792A1 1 0 0 0 3 21z"/><path d="M9.969 17.031 21.378 5.624a1 1 0 0 0-3.002-3.002L6.967 14.031"/></svg>By scheme</span></div><div class="odv-am-lines"><div><b>Pick</b> size.52</div></div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Token</b><div class="odv-am-chain"><code>space.inset.control-x</code><span>→</span><code>padding-x</code><span class="odv-am-val">1.75rem</span><span class="odv-byscheme" title="Its value changes by scheme. The part is the same in every scheme."><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="11" height="11" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m11 10 3 3"/><path d="M6.5 21A3.5 3.5 0 1 0 3 17.5a2.62 2.62 0 0 1-.708 1.792A1 1 0 0 0 3 21z"/><path d="M9.969 17.031 21.378 5.624a1 1 0 0 0-3.002-3.002L6.967 14.031"/></svg>By scheme</span></div><div class="odv-am-lines"><div><b>Pick</b> space.28</div></div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Token</b><div class="odv-am-chain"><code>radius.control</code><span>→</span><code>radius</code><span class="odv-am-val">9999px</span><span class="odv-byscheme" title="Its value changes by scheme. <section class="odv-am-card" id="part-1"><div class="odv-am-img wide"><span class="odv-am-assetbox"><img class="odv-am-asset" src="/anatomy/brand-expressive/button/card-2.png" alt="Emphasis: 1" loading="lazy"/></span></div><div class="odv-am-body"><header><i class="odv-am-n">1</i><b>Emphasis</b><span class="odv-am-role" title="Where does the eye go?">Emphasis</span></header><ul class="odv-am-tree"><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Answer</b><div class="odv-am-main">Color · How many emphasis levels do actions need? → Three</div><div class="odv-am-why">Primary, secondary, ghost.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Rule</b><div class="odv-am-main">For the action that completes the task, use Button primary, large, one per section. Don't use two primaries.</div><div class="odv-am-why">One loud call to action per section.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Rule</b><div class="odv-am-main">For an alternative or cancel, use Button ghost. Don't use a second primary.</div><div class="odv-am-why">The alternative must not compete.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Rule</b><div class="odv-am-main">For delete or remove, use Button secondary, then confirm with Button danger. Don't use button primary.</div><div class="odv-am-why">Confirm before destroying data.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Token</b><div class="odv-am-chain"><code>color.border.strong</code><span>→</span><code>secondary.border</code><span class="odv-am-val">#8A6F63 · dark #B5988A</span><span class="odv-byscheme" title="Its value changes by scheme. The part is the same in every scheme."><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="11" height="11" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m11 10 3 3"/><path d="M6.5 21A3.5 3.5 0 1 0 3 17.5a2.62 2.62 0 0 1-.708 1.792A1 1 0 0 0 3 21z"/><path d="M9.969 17.031 21.378 5.624a1 1 0 0 0-3.002-3.002L6.967 14.031"/></svg>By scheme</span></div><div class="odv-am-why">The edge of a control people must find.</div><div class="odv-am-lines"><div><b>Pick</b> neutral.500: the edge of a control people must find, 4.63:1 on surface.default, above the 3:1 floor.</div><div><b>Dark</b> neutral.400: the edge of a control people must find, 6.71:1 on surface.default, above the 3:1 floor.</div><div><b>Shares the step with</b> category.5, disabled.text. Changing this pick moves only what reads color.border.strong.</div></div></li></ul></div></section>

<section class="odv-am-card" id="part-2"><div class="odv-am-img wide"><span class="odv-am-assetbox"><img class="odv-am-asset" src="/anatomy/brand-expressive/button/card-3.png" alt="Label: 2" loading="lazy"/></span></div><div class="odv-am-body"><header><i class="odv-am-n">2</i><b>Label</b><span class="odv-am-role" title="Can you read it?">Readability</span></header><ul class="odv-am-tree"><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Answer</b><div class="odv-am-main">Typography · Which text roles does it need? → Core and expressive display</div><div class="odv-am-why">A big expressive display role carries the brand.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Answer</b><div class="odv-am-main">Voice and tone · How does it sound? → Playful</div><div class="odv-am-why">Big words, few of them.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Rule</b><div class="odv-am-main">For a button label, use A short verb that moves: Join, Try, Go. The part is the same in every scheme."><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="11" height="11" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m11 10 3 3"/><path d="M6.5 21A3.5 3.5 0 1 0 3 17.5a2.62 2.62 0 0 1-.708 1.792A1 1 0 0 0 3 21z"/><path d="M9.969 17.031 21.378 5.624a1 1 0 0 0-3.002-3.002L6.967 14.031"/></svg>By scheme</span></div><div class="odv-am-why">The fill of the item the pointer or the keyboard is on, or whose submenu is open. A state shows on the item's background, one step from the surface it sits on: darker in light, lighter in dark.</div><div class="odv-am-lines"><div><b>Pick</b> neutral.100, two steps darker than the surfaces it sits on (neutral.0), so the item under the pointer or the keyboard reads as a band without lifting off the page. It skips neutral.50, the page canvas, so a menu item never matches the page behind it.</div><div><b>Dark</b> neutral.100, one step lighter than the surfaces it sits on (neutral.50), so the item under the pointer or the keyboard reads as a band on the menu and on cards.</div><div><b>Shares the step with</b> surface.sunken, action.secondary.hover, category.5.subtle, disabled.surface. Changing this pick moves only what reads color.surface.highlight.</div></div></li></ul></div></section>

## For agents

Agents get this same anatomy: every part, its roles, whether it is required, the tokens it reads and the decisions behind them.

- **From an AI agent:** call the `get_anatomy` tool on the Open DS MCP server, with this scheme and `button`.
- **From a terminal:** `npx open-ds anatomy brand-expressive button`
